name: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
thesis: The world is the totality of facts, not of things.

structure.1: The world is everything that is the case.
structure.2: What is the case—a fact—is the existence of states of affairs.
structure.3: A logical picture of facts is a thought.
structure.4: A thought is a proposition with a sense.
structure.5: A proposition is a truth-function of elementary propositions.
structure.6: The general form of a truth-function is the general form of a proposition.
structure.7: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.

limit.language: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
limit.unsayable: What lies beyond the limits of meaningful proposition is not represented as a fact.

method: Analyze the world into facts, facts into states of affairs, and propositions into their logical form.
source_note: This JSON is a structural paraphrase of the Tractatus, not a transcription or translation of the complete text.
